questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**asleep at the switch**'.

 

**__Key Points__**

• In the given sentence, it describes a **bureaucracy** that is failing to address the critical issue of **youth unemployment**.
 
• The origin of this phrase comes from the **railroad industry**, where a trainman might fail to change a track switch, leading to an accident.

**Complete Sentence:** *When the youth are struggling with unemployment and the bureaucracy is **asleep at the switch**__, how can a great nation be formed?*

**__Additional Information__**

 
• The other options like '**asleep at the light**', '**asleep at the board**', and '**asleep at the cut-out**' are **incorrect variations** and do not constitute standard English idioms.
 
• Common synonyms for being '**asleep at the switch**' include **negligent**, **remiss**, and **oblivious**.

questions.question: Choose the word that is the closest synonym to the word “pulled”.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option (1)** i.e. **Dragged**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'pulled'** means to exert force on someone or something so as to cause movement towards oneself. (**खींचना**)
 
 
• **Example: **She **pulled** the door open to welcome the guests into the house.
 
 
 
• **'Dragged'** refers to pulling someone or something along forcefully, especially with difficulty or along the ground; it is the closest synonym to the word 'pulled' in this context. (**घसीटना**)
 
 
• **Example: **The workers **dragged** the heavy sacks of cement across the construction site.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the synonym of **'pulled'** is **'dragged'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Dragged**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Pushed** (धक्का देना): To exert force on someone or something in order to move them away from oneself.
 
 
• **Example: **He **pushed** the cart through the narrow aisle of the supermarket.
 
 
 
• **Stopped** (रुकना / रोकना): To come to an end or to cause something to cease moving or operating.
 
 
• **Example: **The driver **stopped** the bus at the designated stop.
 
 
 
• **Rejected** (अस्वीकार करना): To dismiss as inadequate, inappropriate, or not meeting certain standards.
 
 
• **Example: **The university **rejected** his application because it was submitted after the deadline.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
They say that honesty is the best policy.

options.text: It is said that honesty is the best policy.
Honesty said to be the best policy.
They are said honesty is the best policy.
Honesty was said to be the best policy.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is said that honesty is the best policy**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• When an active sentence starts with an indefinite subject like **They**, **People**, or **Someone** followed by a reporting verb (e.g., **say**, **think**, **believe**) and a **that-clause**, the passive voice is often introduced by the **dummy subject** **It**.

• The active verb **say** is in the **Present Indefinite Tense**. To convert this into the passive voice, we use the structure: **It + is + past participle (V3) + that-clause**.

• In this specific sentence, **They say** becomes **It is said**. The **conjunction** **that** connects the passive introductory phrase to the rest of the statement.

• The phrase **honesty is the best policy** is a **universal truth** and a **noun clause** acting as the object. In such constructions, the content of the **that-clause** remains unchanged during the transformation.

• Therefore, the complete passive construction is **It is said that honesty is the best policy**.

 **Additional Information__**

• Comparison of incorrect options:

• **Honesty said to be the best policy**: This is grammatically incomplete as it lacks the **auxiliary verb** (is) necessary to form the **Passive Voice**.

• **They are said honesty is the best policy**: This structure is logically and syntactically incorrect because the **pronoun** **They** cannot be the subject of the passive verb **are said** while simultaneously retaining the noun clause in this manner.

• **Honesty was said to be the best policy**: This is incorrect because it changes the **tense** of the original sentence. The reporting verb **say** is in the present tense, so the passive form must use **is** rather than the past tense **was**.

• Alternative Passive Structure:

• Such sentences can also be converted using the **Subject + Verb (Passive) + To-infinitive** pattern. For example: **Honesty is said to be the best policy**. This involves moving the **subject** of the noun clause to the start of the sentence.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
Is a complete health check-up provided by the insurance company every year?

options.text: Does the insurance company provide a complete health check-up every year?
Is the insurance company providing a complete health check-up every year?
Did the insurance company provide a complete health check-up every year?
Has the insurance company provided a complete health check-up every year?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Does the insurance company provide a complete health check-up every year?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the structure of an interrogative sentence in the **Present Simple Tense**. This is identified by the auxiliary verb **'Is'** at the beginning and the **Past Participle** form of the verb **'provided'**.

• The phrase **'every year'** acts as an adverbial of frequency, which is a hallmark of the **Present Simple Tense**, indicating a habitual or routine action.

• To convert an interrogative sentence from passive to **Active Voice** in this tense, we use the formula: **Do/Does + Subject + Base Verb (V1) + Object?**.

• The **Passive Agent** 'the insurance company' becomes the **Active Subject**. Since 'the insurance company' is a singular third-person entity, the auxiliary verb **'Does'** must be used.

• The **Passive Subject** 'a complete health check-up' becomes the **Active Object**, and the verb 'provided' reverts to its base form, **'provide'**.

 **Additional Information__**

• Understanding Tense Variations in Interrogative Sentences:

• **Present Continuous Tense**: Uses the structure 'Is/Am/Are + Subject + V-ing?'. It is used for actions happening at the moment of speaking.

• **Past Simple Tense**: Uses 'Did + Subject + V1?'. This is used to inquire about actions that were completed at a specific time in the past.

• **Present Perfect Tense**: Uses 'Has/Have + Subject + V3?'. This tense is typically used for actions where the time is not specific or the action has relevance to the present.

• **Active Voice** emphasizes the **doer** of the action, making the sentence more direct and clear, whereas **Passive Voice** emphasizes the **recipient** or the action itself.

</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
The meeting had already started, and several key decisions were made by the time the new director arrived.

options.text: several key decisions had been made

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes a sequence of events in the **past**. When two actions happen in the past, the action that was completed first is expressed in the **Past Perfect Tense** (had + past participle).
 
• The phrase **by the time** is a strong indicator that the **Past Perfect** should be used to show that the decisions were finished before the director's arrival.
 
• Since the **decisions** are the recipients of the action, the **Passive Voice** of the Past Perfect is required: **had been + past participle (made)**.
 
• Therefore, the underlined part **were made** should be replaced with **had been made** to correctly reflect the timeline of events.

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'The meeting had already started, and **several key decisions had been made** by the time the new director arrived.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "several keys decision were made"** – This is grammatically incorrect because **keys** is used as an adjective here and should be singular (**key**), and **decision** should be plural (**decisions**) to match the quantifier **several**.
 
• **Option 3: "several keen decisions was made"** – This contains a **subject-verb agreement** error; the plural subject **decisions** requires the plural verb **were** or **had been**, not the singular **was**. Additionally, **keen** changes the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "No improvement required"** – This is incorrect because the **Simple Past** (were made) does not clearly establish the completion of the action before the director's arrival as accurately as the **Past Perfect** does in a formal grammatical context.
</ul

A person who is stubborn and refuses to compromise.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **A person who is unsuited for a particular position, role, or situation.**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **'A square peg in a round hole'** refers to an individual who does not fit into a particular environment, social group, or job role because their character or skills are not appropriate for it. (**अनुपयुक्त व्यक्ति**)
 
 
• **Example: **He felt like a **square peg in a round hole** when he joined the high-pressure financial firm, as he was much more interested in the arts.
 
 
 
• **'A person who is unsuited for a particular position, role, or situation'** describes a state of mismatch where a person's personality or abilities are not aligned with the requirements of their situation. (**एक व्यक्ति जो किसी विशेष पद, भूमिका या स्थिति के लिए अनुपयुक्त है**)
 
 
• **Example: **Placing a shy, quiet person in a loud public relations job is a classic example of a **square peg in a round hole**.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct meaning of the given idiom is someone who is a misfit in their role.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **A person who is unsuited for a particular position, role, or situation.**

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **A person who secretly dislikes their coworkers** (सहकर्मियों के प्रति गुप्त द्वेष रखने वाला व्यक्ति): This refers to internal feelings of animosity toward colleagues, which is not the meaning of the idiom.
 
 
• **Example: **Despite his polite behavior, he was known to be **a person who secretly dislikes his coworkers**.
 
 
 
• **A person who is physically awkward or uncoordinated** (शारीरिक रूप से अनाड़ी या असमन्वित व्यक्ति): This describes someone who is clumsy in their movements.
 
 
• **Example: **His frequent tripping made him seem like **a person who is physically awkward**.
 
 
 
• **A person who is stubborn and refuses to compromise** (हठी व्यक्ति जो समझौता करने से इनकार करता है): This describes a person who is inflexible or headstrong in their opinions.
 
 
• **Example: **The project was delayed because the manager was **a person who is stubborn and refuses to compromise**.

In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. A mother loves her son from the moment he is born. 

P. She takes care of him as he grows and learns new things. 

Q. She supports him in school and encourages him to follow his dreams. 

R. She protects him from dangers and teaches him good values. 

S. She guides him during difficult times with patience and wisdom. 

6. Her love remains strong even when he becomes an adult.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The passage outlines the lifelong journey and the evolving role of a **mother** in her **son's** life, following a chronological and logical progression from infancy to maturity. 
• **Sentence 1** establishes the starting point of the bond: **birth**. 
• **Sentence P follows** as the first stage of the child's development, focusing on the basic physical care required as he **grows** and **learns** about the world. 
• **Sentence R follows** because it describes the mother's next role as a **protector** and a mentor who instills **good values** during the child's early developmental years. 
• **Sentence Q is the fourth sentence** as it transitions to a more social and structured stage of life, highlighting the mother's support during his **school** years and her encouragement of his **dreams**. 
• **Sentence S follows** as it addresses the mother's support during the emotional challenges and **difficult times** that occur as the child matures, requiring **patience** and **wisdom**. 
• **Sentence 6** provides the conclusion, stating that this unwavering **love** persists into his **adulthood**. 
• The correct sequence is **PRQS**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'A mother loves her son from the moment he is born. She takes care of him as he grows and learns new things. She protects him from dangers and teaches him good values. She supports him in school and encourages him to follow his dreams. She guides him during difficult times with patience and wisdom. Her love remains strong even when he becomes an adult.'</div
